page: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The hardware profile features 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 256.0 GB, providing an 8.0 GB allocation per vCPU alongside a 105 MB L3 cache. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. There is no bundled local ephemeral storage, meaning all persistent and temporary disk operations require attached network block storage. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Performance testing reflects strong compute and decompression capabilities. The instance achieved an upper-quartile Geekbench single-core score of 2210.0 and a multi-core score of 18347.0, supported by strong gzip single-threaded compression (33.05 GB/sec) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (210.74 GB/sec). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 182.67 GB/sec, placing in the middle 50% tier. Small model text generation for lightweight 135M parameter LLMs scored in the top tier at 343.5 tokens/sec, but processing degraded to 2.74 tokens/sec on large 70B parameter models, confirming hardware bounds on larger AI inferencing tasks.

Cost efficiency is centered around its memory-dense profile. By eliminating the expense of integrated local NVMe arrays and specialized accelerator hardware, the server balances compute performance with large RAM allocations. However, applications requiring low-latency scratch space will incur additional network storage overhead. The configuration is primarily tailored to in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving infrastructure, and memory-intensive data compression pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor clocked at 4.0 GHz. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance pairs 256.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) with 105 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions. No integrated local storage or GPU accelerators are included, requiring reliance on remote block storage for data persistence. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core and multi-core processing in Geekbench, rapid bzip3 decompression, and high static web serving throughput, while memory bandwidth and PassMark operational scores sit in the median tier. By omitting high-cost local NVMe tiers and GPUs, the instance delivers predictable compute and memory density for memory-intensive workloads including in-memory databases, Redis cache deployments, and compression pipelines.
